replacement: ANNE. Set down, set down your honorable load, if honor can be wrapped in a coffin, while I mourn for a while, as is my duty, the untimely fall of virtuous Lancaster. Poor, key-cold body of a holy king. Pale ashes of the house of Lancaster. You bloodless remnant of that royal blood. Let me call on your ghost to hear the laments of poor Anne, wife to your Edward, your slaughtered son. He was stabbed by the same hand that made these wounds. Look, into these windows that let out your life I pour the helpless balm of my poor eyes. Oh, cursed be the hand that made these holes. Cursed be the heart that had the heart to do it. Cursed be the blood that let this blood out. May worse misfortune fall on that hated wretch who makes us wretched by your death than I can wish on adders, spiders, toads or any creeping, venomous thing alive. If he ever has a child, may it be born dead, monstrous and before its time, with an ugly, unnatural look that may frighten its hopeful mother at the sight, and may that child inherit his unhappiness. If he ever has a wife, may she be made more miserable by his death than I am by the death of my young lord and you. Now go on toward Chertsey with your holy load, taken from Saint Paul's to be buried there. And whenever you are tired of the weight, rest, while I mourn King Henry's body.

RICHARD. Meanwhile, God grants that we do need your help. Our brother is imprisoned by your doing, I am disgraced, and the nobility are held in contempt, while great promotions are handed out every day to ennoble people who were barely worth a single noble coin two days ago.
RIVERS. She may, my lord, for —

RICHARD. She may, Lord Rivers! Why, who doesn't know that? She may do more than deny it, sir. She may help you to many fine promotions, and then deny that she lent a hand, and credit those honors to your own great merit. What may she not do? She may, yes, indeed, she may —

SECOND CITIZEN. There is hope that he will govern well. While he's a minor, a council will govern under him. When he's fully grown, he will govern himself. I have no doubt he will govern well, both then and until then.
CATESBY. Both Dukes think highly of you —
HASTINGS. If they have done this deed, my noble lord —
BUCKINGHAM. Lord Mayor, the reason we have sent —

BUCKINGHAM. My lord, this shows conscience in your Grace. But the scruples behind it are petty and trivial, once everything is considered. You say that Edward is your brother's son. So do we, but not by Edward's wife. He was first contracted to Lady Lucy, and your mother is alive to witness his vow. Afterward he was betrothed by proxy to Bona, sister of the King of France. He broke off both. Then a poor petitioner, a mother of many sons worn out with cares, a widow whose beauty was fading and who was in distress, in the afternoon of her best days, became the prize and purchase of his lustful eye. That eye seduced the height and pitch of his rank down to a base decline and a loathsome bigamy. By her, in his unlawful bed, he fathered this Edward, whom we politely call the Prince. I could complain more bitterly, but out of respect for some who are still alive, I put a limit on my tongue. So, my good lord, take this offered dignity for yourself. If not to bless us and the land, then at least to draw your noble ancestry out of the corruption of abusing times and back onto a true line of descent.
There you will be crowned Richard's royal queen.
SECOND MESSENGER. In Kent, my lord, the Guilfords are in arms. Every hour more allies flock to the rebels, and their strength grows.
RICHMOND. God and your arms be praised, victorious friends! The day is ours. The bloody dog is dead.
